plain_description.what: Replays three judging policies on 9,142 cached matches that store both presentation orders: always judge in both orders, always one order, or both orders only when the two models' answers differ. No calls.
plain_description.why: Judging each pair in both orders doubles the cost. The test asks whether the second order can be skipped when the answers already agree.
plain_description.information: Same quality at fewer calls would be a cheap saving. Result: done, registered failure. The selective policy costs 58% more than single order and gives the same weaker leaderboard (0.958 vs 0.972). Orders disagree more often on agreeing answers (19% vs 11%). There, a single order invents a winner and usually favours the longer answer. There is no cheap subset to skip. Arena-pool data, later ruled history, not evidence.
